name: Schedar
description: A star 70 parsecs away, 41 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: radius 41.078 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 733.504 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: effective temperature 4690 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: distance 69.979 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.01), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 70 parsecs away, 41 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 734 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,690 K, so 41.078 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 3179: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alpha Cassiopeiae
quotes.card: Alpha Cassiopeiae is a star in the northern constellation of Cassiopeia.
quotes.introduction: Though listed as the "alpha star" by Johann Bayer, α Cas's visual brightness closely matches the 'beta' (β) star in the constellation and it may appear marginally brighter or dimmer, depending on which passband is used.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 418551920284673408 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
